newsitem.title: USA: Crude strength to fuel oil majors' first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Crude strength to fuel oil majors' first quarter.

text.p: The first quarter of 1997 will see double-digit earnings growth for major oil companies, mostly in the high-teens to low twenty percent range when they report next week, analysts say.

"The first half of the first quarter will show the benefit of strong crude prices on upstream operations, but refining and marketing operations will not show many benefits of this," said Chris Stavros, analyst at Prudential Securities.

The price for the benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude blend has risen to $23.27 in the first quarter from $19.68 a year ago, while average U.S. refining and marketing margins have slid to $5.48 from $6.56.

Among majors, Texaco Inc's first quarter is seen up 21 percent and Exxon Corp is expected to report a 17 percent rise on Monday, while Mobil Corp is seen up 10 percent when it releases earnings on Wednesday.

"It is a question of business mix, those companies that are more highly leveraged to oil and gas will do better, those with a large chemical component will suffer to some extent because prices are down from the first quarter of 1996," said Steve Pfeifer, analyst at PaineWebber.

This means that Amoco Corp is seen flat to slightly lower, largely as a result of its chemical operations, while Unocal Corp earnings per share growth is expected to be close to 58 percent over the year-ago quarter.

USX-Marathon Group is seen posting a healthy 48.7 percent gain in the first quarter to $0.58 per share from $0.39 and Oppenheimer & Co earlier this month raised its earnings per share outlook to $0.60 from $0.52 on improved refining margins in the Midwest region.
Oppenheimer expects refining and marketing after tax earnings at Marathon's refining division to rise to $65 million in the first quarter from $44 million a year ago.

Looking further out, most analysts believe that there will be some weakness in crude prices, especially in the third quarter of 1997 as refineries wind down production as demand from car users begins to subside.
"There may be some price strength in the fourth quarter of 1997, but that is not guaranteed," said Prudential's Stavros.

The refining and marketing sector, which has been plagued by low profitability and defensive mergers, is not expected to show many benefits from steady to declining crude oil prices through the year as overcapacity continues to be the major factor.

"If there is any hope on the refining and marketing sector, then it may come from the independents in the second quarter, but if demand does not hold up, there will be renewed pressure on margins," said Stavros.
